newsitem.title: INDIA: India says committed to cutting fiscal deficit.
newsitem.headline: India says committed to cutting fiscal deficit.

text.p: The Indian government said on Tuesday that it remains committed to reducing the fiscal deficit as a share of gross domestic product (GDP).
"It is essential to keep reducing the Centre's fiscal deficit to below four percent of GDP as soon as possible," it said in the annual Economic Survey.

The survey said reductions in the fiscal deficit would help to push down interest rates, free up resources for invesment, check inflation, curb interest payment, facilitate the development of a market for long-term debt securities and reduce the risks associated with excessive borrowing from external sources.

The survey did not give an estimate of the 1996/97 (April-March) fiscal deficit as a share of GDP. It repeated the target which the government set last year of 5.0 percent of GDP, down from 5.8 percent in 1995/96.
